turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm trying to cut our grocery bill and I can't decide where to do the weekly shop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want your opinion, but only after you've heard every option. I'll say when I'm done.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our usual big supermarket has everything in one place and good loyalty points, but I always overspend there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The discount shop across town is way cheaper, though the range is small and it's a twenty minute drive.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We could do online delivery, no impulse buys, but there's a fee and sometimes they swap things.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or the Saturday market for veg and the corner shop for the rest, which is fun but takes ages.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm done. What do you think?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A mix could work best. Do a big monthly stock up at the discount shop for basics, and order the rest online so you dodge the treats aisle. Keep the market for a weekend treat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Changing the subject, I've been training for two months and the scale hasn't moved. I'm so frustrated.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's understandable. But the scale is only one measure, and if you're lifting, you might be building muscle as you lose fat.
